inputs.share_count_basis: 3,120.2m stapled securities on issue (FY2026 annual report, security-holder information) plus ~1m unvested performance awards; held flat. DRP issuance (~0.4%/yr historically) is at market price and treated as value-neutral.
inputs.cash_note: ESTIMATE. Transurban does not publish proportional cash. Statutory cash 2,060 (FY2026 balance sheet) plus 50% of the 932 held by the equity-accounted STP JV / NWRG / Transurban Chesapeake (note B20, 100% basis) less an assumed ~125 for the minority share of cash in the 62.5%/75.1%-owned consolidated groups. A +/-300 error is +/-0.10 per security.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: UNLEVERED proportional free cash, built here, not a company-reported line: proportional operating EBITDA 3,063 + 16 SBC add-back - 60 proportional income taxes paid - 121 non-maintenance capex (3% of revenue). The company's own 'Free Cash' (2,111, 67.7 cps) is after 897 of net finance costs and is NOT the base for this EV model; statutory OCF less capex (1,335) is a consolidated, post-interest figure that excludes the equity-accounted roads.
inputs.interest_income_note: Flows are unlevered (before all net finance costs), so interest income is already outside them; the cash that earns it is in net debt.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 annual report cash-flow reconciliation, 'Non-cash employee benefits expense - share based payments' 16 (FY2025 14). Proportional EBITDA is struck after this expense, so the EBITDA margin path is grossed up by 0.4pp and SBC charged on its own row - charged once.
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD build, 7.0% for every scenario (risk is charged in the flows and weights, not in per-scenario discount rates). Cost of equity ~8.5% (AU 10-year government bond ~4.4% + 0.75 beta x 5.5% ERP); cost of debt 4.8% = the FY2026 weighted average cost of AUD debt, taken PRE-tax because the flows deduct actual cash tax, which already carries the interest shield (capital-cash-flow consistency); weights 63% equity / 37% debt per reported gearing of 37.4%. 0.63 x 8.5 + 0.37 x 4.8 = 7.1, rounded to 7.0 to match the folder's regulated-infrastructure precedent (APA.AX).
inputs.lease_treatment: Immaterial: lease liabilities 31 (FY2026). Lease costs stay inside post-IFRS-16 EBITDA and lease liabilities are left out of net debt; no adjustment either way.
inputs.nci_treatment: PROPORTIONAL basis throughout: revenue, EBITDA, tax, debt and cash are all Transurban's ownership share of each road (note B4), so minorities in Transurban Queensland / Eastern Distributor are already excluded and the 50%-owned WestConnex, NWRG and Greater Washington roads are already included. No NCI deduction and no equity-accounted-investment add-back in the bridge - either would double count.
inputs.terminal_note: Concessions are FINITE (revenue-weighted remaining life ~27 years at FY2026; individual roads 2035-2087), so a Gordon perpetuity is wrong in principle. The terminal_cap_multiple is set to the growing-annuity factor for the concession life remaining at year 10 and is the binding constraint in every scenario; terminal_growth only feeds the non-binding Gordon leg, so the terminal-growth axis of the sensitivity grid is flat by construction.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF with the non-US adaptations, run on Transurban's PROPORTIONAL (ownership-share) accounts as an unlevered enterprise valuation less proportional net debt. Routing: the dcf-methods table has no infrastructure row; Transurban is an operating company (toll collection under concession deeds), not a REIT/LIC/bank, so it routes to owner-FCF + adaptations, as APA.AX did. Statutory accounts are unusable as the base - they consolidate 100% of 62.5%/75.1%-owned roads and equity-account WestConnex, M7/NorthConnex and the US Express Lanes (931 of 3,110 proportional EBITDA), and statutory revenue carries construction revenue. A post-interest 'Free Cash at cost of equity' capitalisation was rejected: Free Cash is struck before debt repayment, and every dollar of the 27.1bn of debt must be repaid out of a finite concession life, which an equity-yield capitalisation ignores. Proportional operating EBITDA is already after cash major-maintenance spend, so the only capex in the flows is ~3% of revenue for tolling technology and corporate PPE; growth projects (Logan West, M2-M7 widening, I-95 bi-directional) and the announced 4.5bn debt-funded purchase of CPP Investments' NWRG/STP stakes (completion expected calendar 2027) are EXCLUDED as value-neutral - neither their debt nor their cash flows are in the model. Not adjusted: the 35.0 cps final distribution paid 18 August 2026 (~1,092) left the 30 June cash balance, roughly offset by 4.5 months of FY2027 flows the end-of-year discounting does not credit; the ConnectEast litigation liability (143 booked FY2025). SBC is 0.4% of revenue so the house/street band is ~0.13 a security wide; band_position is therefore a meaningless large number (price far outside a near-zero band) and should be read as n/a. ENTRY PRICE CAVEAT: the 15% hurdle is applied to unlevered flows of an asset carrying ~25bn of debt at under 5%; it leaves almost nothing for equity and is not a realistic buy-below price for a leveraged infrastructure security - read the required-return table instead. Price is the last regular close before the valuation date (a weekend).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: CPI-linked toll escalation (~3%) plus ~1.5-2% traffic growth; cross-checked to the 10-year distribution-per-security CAGR of 4.3% (45.5 -> 69.0 cps)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is negative and unusable (distributions exceed statutory profit by design; book equity shrinks as concession intangibles amortise) and statutory EPS is noise (FY2021 carries a 3.3bn disposal gain). Both diverge by far more than 30% from revenue. Growth is selected from the toll-escalation mechanics instead.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue = proportional toll revenue (FY2023 3,314, FY2021 2,486, FY2026 3,982); the 5-year figure starts from a COVID-depressed base and includes the WestConnex stake step-ups. FCF = company Free Cash excluding capital releases (FY2023 1,725, FY2021 939, FY2026 2,111), the only consistently published cash series; it is post-interest, so it is a growth cross-check only and not the model base. SBC (14-16 a year) is immaterial to any of these series.

base.growth_note: FY2027-28 carry the M5 West step-down (100% -> 50% from December 2026; management quantifies it as ~2.3% off the four-year Free Cash CAGR, i.e. ~6% of EBITDA, split ~7 months / 5 months) against ~6% underlying growth from escalation, traffic (+3.1% in the September 2026 quarter) and the West Gate Tunnel / M7-M12 / 495 Northern Extension ramp. FY2035-36 trimmed for the Cross City Tunnel expiry (2035).
base.ebitda_margin_note: Pre-SBC. FY2026 actual 76.1% (3,063 + 16 over 4,047). Flat for two years as the high-margin M5 West half leaves, then +20-40bp a year on management's below-inflation cost growth against CPI-linked revenue.
base.da_pct_note: Only matters for the tax base. Proportional D&A is not published; ~40% of revenue is estimated from statutory D&A of 1,162 adjusted for minorities and the equity-accounted roads. It drifts down as revenue escalates over a fixed concession base.
base.cash_tax_rate_note: Rate on EBIT that reproduces ACTUAL proportional cash tax after the interest shield and the trust structure: FY2026 60 paid on ~1,400 of EBIT = 4.3%. Ramps to 17% as depreciation shields roll off and corporate-entity tax becomes payable; the trust leg stays untaxed at entity level, which is why it does not reach 30%.
base.terminal_cap_note: Growing-annuity factor for ~18 years of remaining revenue-weighted concession life at FY2036 (CityLink 2045, Sydney ex-WestConnex 2048, Brisbane 2051-65, WestConnex 2060, US 2087), cash flows escalating 4%, discounted at 7%: ~13.9x.

bull.terminal_cap_note: ~24 years of effective remaining life at FY2036: concession extensions granted in exchange for upgrade capex (the CityLink extension for West Gate Tunnel and the M7 extension for M7-M12 are the precedents) plus a larger share of value in the 2060 and 2087 concessions.

bear.terminal_cap_note: ~16 years of remaining life at FY2036 with cash flows escalating only 2.5% and no concession extensions: ~11x.

scenario_narratives.base: Tolls escalate with CPI (CityLink at its fixed 4.25% until 2029) and traffic grows 1.5-2% a year on population growth, with the West Gate Tunnel, M7-M12 and the 495 Northern Extension still ramping. FY2027 and FY2028 absorb the halving of the M5 West interest, which is why distribution coverage dips below the 95-105% target. The NSW Direct Deal proves value-neutral as management states. Costs grow below inflation, lifting the margin about two points over the decade. Cash tax, negligible today, climbs steadily as depreciation shields unwind. No concession is extended, and the roads are valued for the ~18 years of life left at FY2036.
scenario_narratives.bull: Traffic on the new capacity ramps faster than planned, the US Express Lanes keep compounding at double digits on dynamic pricing, and the NSW toll cuts stimulate enough volume to more than pay for themselves. Operating leverage takes the margin to ~79.5%. Most importantly, governments keep trading concession extensions for upgrade capex (Logan West, M2-M7, I-95 bi-directional), as they did for West Gate Tunnel and M7-M12, so the effective remaining life at FY2036 is ~24 years rather than 18.
scenario_narratives.bear: Cost-of-living pressure and working-from-home hold traffic growth near 1%, inflation sits at the bottom of the target band so escalation runs ~2.5%, and the Direct Deal toll cuts are not recovered in volume. Margins drift down as tolling technology, cyber and insurance costs outpace revenue. Road-user-charging reform and political pressure on tolls mean no concession is extended and escalation terms are not improved; tax shields unwind faster. Refinancing 27bn of debt at higher rates does not appear in these unlevered flows but is the reason the bear weight is raised.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: equity is a thin residual over ~25bn of net debt, revenue terms rest on a handful of state governments (the NSW reform has just shown tolls can be reset), and funding costs are rising (AUD debt cost 4.5% -> 4.8% in a year). Base 50%: contracted escalation makes the central path unusually visible. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs faster traffic, margin expansion AND further concession extensions, three separate things going right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Transurban is a finite-life, CPI-linked annuity financed with a great deal of long-dated debt. It is valued as the present value of its ownership share of unlevered road cash flows over the concession life, less its share of the debt. Because equity is the residual of a ~50bn asset over ~25bn of net debt, each 0.5pp of discount rate moves value per security by well over a dollar: the answer is dominated by the discount rate and by whether concessions are extended, not by the traffic forecast. The market price implies an asset return near 5% (or concession lives that keep being extended); the house 7% does not get there.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount-rate sensitivity: with 37% gearing the equity value is roughly twice as sensitive to WACC as the enterprise value; but the discount rate alone does not close the gap - with the 14x terminal cap held, a 5% WACC still gives only ~12 a security, so the price needs both a low rate and longer effective concession lives.
Concession extensions are worth several dollars a security and are excluded from the base case; the terminal cap multiple (11x / 14x / 17x) is the single most important driver.
Proportional cash (2,400) and proportional D&A (~40% of revenue) are estimates - neither is disclosed.
The 4.5bn CPP Investments stake purchase and the development pipeline are treated as value-neutral; an acquisition priced at the market's ~5% asset return would be value-dilutive on this model's 7%.
Cash tax is ~2% of EBITDA today; the pace at which it normalises is a judgment with little disclosure behind it.
Regulatory: NSW Direct Deal outcome, road-user charging, and the precedent either sets for other states.
